Threat.value: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
I notice potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
The memory feels like it is happening right now rather than something that is over
The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened
The world is a dangerous place
My body has been permanently damaged by what happened

vignette: Seventy-year-old Carlos Hernandez still remembers the chill in the air that night. A prosecutor for over three decades, he had always prided himself on his ability to remain calm and collected under pressure. But nothing could have prepared him for the sexual assault that took place in a parking garage near his office building. It was a cold winter evening, and as he walked back to his car, a stranger emerged from the shadows and attacked him. The details of that night are still etched vividly in Carlos's mind - the sound of footsteps echoing off the concrete walls, the feel of icy air on his skin, and the overwhelming sense of helplessness. As he lies awake at night, he can almost smell the dampness of the garage and taste the fear that grips him. Since then, certain triggers have become impossible for Carlos to ignore. Being around children is particularly distressing - their laughter and playful shouts somehow transport him back to that fateful night. He's had to limit his interactions with his grandchildren, much to his own dismay. Even specific temperatures can evoke a visceral response; the slightest chill on his skin makes him recoil in discomfort. Carlos has become increasingly vigilant about his surroundings. He avoids unfamiliar places, hesitant to venture into new environments where he can't assess potential dangers. When he enters any room or building, he instinctively scans for exits - it's an automatic reflex now, a constant reminder that safety is never guaranteed. His eyes are drawn to objects that could be used as weapons: a broken bottle on the floor, a heavy bookend on a shelf. Memories of the assault intrude into his daily life with unsettling regularity. The recollections feel incredibly vivid and present - it's as if he's reliving the experience all over again. He can't shake off the sense that it's happening in real-time, rather than being a distant memory. These flashbacks force their way into his consciousness at the most inopportune moments: during meetings, while walking down the street, or even when he's alone with loved ones. Carlos has come to believe that he's been irreparably damaged by what happened - his body, once strong and resilient, now feels vulnerable and fragile. He can't shake off the feeling of contamination - as if some part of him remains tainted by the assault. The world seems a more treacherous place than it ever did before; every stranger is a potential threat, every public space a possible trap. The consequences of his symptoms have accumulated over time, taking a toll on both his personal and professional life. He's become increasingly withdrawn, hesitant to engage with colleagues or socialize outside work. His performance as a prosecutor has suffered - he finds himself preoccupied by thoughts of safety and vulnerability, rather than focusing on the cases at hand. As Carlos navigates this new reality, he can't help but wonder if things will ever return to normal. What finally brought him to seek help was his growing concern about his ability to keep up with his work - a role that once gave him purpose now feels like an insurmountable challenge. He's terrified of losing the one thing that still defines him: his sense of self-worth as a prosecutor. As he sits in his armchair, staring out into the darkness, Carlos is aware of the vast chasm between who he used to be and who he's become. It's this abyss that scares him most - will therapy help him bridge it, or will it remain an insurmountable gulf?
